neet_che_u02_t11_1.working: Filling order is 4s, then 3d (n+l = 5, lower n than 4p), then 4p.

neet_che_u02_t11_2.working: n+l values: 6p = 7, 5d = 7, 4f = 7, 6s = 6. When n+l is tied, higher n means higher energy, so 6p is highest.

neet_che_u02_t11_3.working: Co is [Ar]3d7 4s2. Seven d electrons in five orbitals give 3 unpaired.

neet_che_u02_t11_4.working: Pairing begins after half-filling: p with the 4th electron, d with the 6th, f with the 8th. An orbital holds at most 2 electrons. So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

neet_che_u02_t11_5.working: A is true (4s n+l = 4 vs 3d n+l = 5). B is false (Hund's rule applies to degenerate orbitals, not 1s/2s). C is true. D is false (5s fills before 4d). E is true (Fe2+ is [Ar]3d6). Correct set: A, C, E.
